threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it 'The Overground,' not just a train to Hackney. You still think it’s a fashionable area instead of just home.
Caught a glimpse of a lad singing to his thumb guitar- didn't know you could strum 'Wonderwall' in a bus seat. Everyone just nodded along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a quiet café on a side street with the best homemade vegan cake, I knew Neukölln had become my home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find an art installation in an old toilet building, showcasing local artists while serving as a quirky gallery.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they snag a burrito during a BART delay without missing a beat, while newcomers just stare at the chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo napping on the 14 today, clutching a bouquet. Guess even weddings can turn into Muni adventures.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we spend all day in cafes. But locals know the real charm is in the late-night chats on the street—with just the right light from the lampposts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still fumble with the metro map, asking for directions in English as if it’s a tourist attraction.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still taking photos of the street art, instead of walking past it like it’s the daily wallpaper.
Caught a late 333 last week; a guy was serenading the whole bus with a ukulele. Didn't know if I should join in or get off at the next stop!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of fresh döner and currywurst mixed with the sound of street musicians on Sonnenallee at midnight. That’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous dance party at a bus stop during a BVG strike. It somehow turns the chaos into a community fest.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they greet the taco truck guy like an old friend, while the newcomers just stare at the menu.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a Muni driver hand a sandwich to a homeless guy at 16th Street. That’s the kind of empathy you don’t see enough in this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love vermut. I've seen many turn their noses up at the stuff, preferring a simple canya instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their reluctance to embrace the siesta; you’ll see them hustling around at 3 PM, while locals linger over coffee.
